A matrix has an order, number of rows by number of columns. Two matrices are conformable for addition or subtraction only when both orders match. For equal order matrices ay and B, the entry in row i, column j of ay plus B is a i j plus b i j, in ay minus B it is a i j minus b i j. The result has the same order. A determinant is a quick test for whether a square matrix can be undone by an inverse. For a two times two matrix, it takes one subtraction.

For ay equals the two by two matrix with first row a, b, and second row c, d, evaluate the two times two determinant as the determinant of ay equals a d minus b c, the main diagonal product minus the other diagonal product. A matrix is singular exactly when its determinant is zero, then it has no inverse. It is non singular when its determinant is nonzero, then an inverse exists. A zero entry by itself does not make a matrix singular. For example, the two by two matrix with first row zero, one, and second row one, zero has determinant minus one and is non singular.

In one breath.
Matrix addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication work entry by entry. Products use rows against columns, while the determinant tells you whether a two times two matrix can be inverted.
Key ideas.

A matrix is a rectangular array with an order, rows by columns. Matrices are conformable for addition or subtraction only if they have the same order. Add or subtract entries in corresponding positions. For example, the top right entry of ay minus B is a twelve minus b twelve, never b twelve minus a twelve unless the question asks for B minus ay.

Scalar multiplication applies to every entry, if ay equals the two by two matrix with first row a, b, and second row c, d, then k ay equals the two by two matrix with first row k a, k b, and second row k c, k d. It distributes over matrix addition, k open bracket ay plus B close bracket equals k ay plus k B. This lets you simplify linear combinations such as two ay minus three B by scaling both matrices first, then subtracting corresponding entries.

For a matrix product ay B, the number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B. Thus a two times three matrix times a three times four matrix gives a two times four matrix. To obtain entry open bracket i, j close bracket, multiply row i of ay by column j of B and add the products. Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative, ay B and B A may differ, and one may not even exist. You may regroup compatible products because multiplication is associative, open bracket ay B close bracket C equals A open bracket B C close bracket.

For ay equals the two by two matrix with first row a, b, and second row c, d, its determinant is the determinant of ay equals a d minus b c. A matrix is singular if its determinant is zero, and non singular if its determinant is nonzero. Only a non singular matrix has an inverse. When a d minus b c is not equal to zero.

Method.
Before adding or subtracting, check that the orders match. Before multiplying, check the inner dimensions, write down the outer dimensions of the result.
For addition, subtraction or scalar multiplication, work at matching positions. For a product, take each required row column dot product and preserve the factor order.
For a two times two inverse, calculate a d minus b c first. If it is zero, state that no inverse exists. Otherwise swap a, d, negate b, c, and divide the whole matrix by the determinant.
If the expression is open bracket ay B close bracket to the minus one, invert the factors and reverse their order. Multiply back to the identity if asked to verify.

Traps.
Trap, Adding matrices with different orders. Why it's wrong, Corresponding positions cannot all be paired. Instead, Check both row and column counts first.

Trap, Multiplying matrices entrywise, or assuming ay B equals B ay. Why it's wrong, Products are built from row column dot products and factor order matters. Instead, Check inner dimensions and keep the written order.

Trap, Using a d plus b c or inverting a singular matrix. Why it's wrong, The determinant is a d minus b c, and zero would cause division by zero. Instead, Calculate the determinant before applying the inverse formula.

Trap, Writing open bracket ay B close bracket to the minus one equals ay to the minus one B to the minus one. Why it's wrong, The adjacent factors will not generally cancel. Instead, Reverse the order to B to the minus one ay to the minus one.
